title: TCP SYN flood
text:
Sudden spikes in incoming SYN packets to SCADA MAPS system - Filter used: tcp.flags.syn == 1 && tcp.flags.ack == 0




22392  26.607391   192.168.127.126 192.168.127.6   TCP 60  61202 → 445 [SYN] Seq=0 Win=1024 Len=0 MSS=1460
22395  26.607760   192.168.127.6   192.168.127.126 TCP 60  445 → 61202 [SYN, ACK] Seq=0 Ack=1 Win=64240 Len=0 MSS=1460 #### SYN-ACK - It tells the client that the endpoint is listening and that the connection can proceed to the final ACK, so it is a core signal in normal session establishment as well as in reconnaissance. - Because the exchange happens before application data flows, defenders often treat SYN-ACK traffic as an early indicator of reachable services, exposed ports, and connection attempts that merit closer inspection.


When a service returns SYN-ACK, it confirms that something is reachable at the network and transport layers. That makes the handshake useful to administrators, but also to attackers who are mapping live hosts, confirming open ports, or identifying services that respond consistently under scan pressure.



SynAck is a low-level control point that attackers can use for both discovery and disruption. A service that answers too predictably to scanning can expose its presence, while a service that must maintain many half-open connections can be pressured into wasting resources. - Failure mechanism: Attackers exploit the gap between SYN and the final ACK to confirm reachability, map exposed services, or consume server-side connection state before a session is established. - Impact: The result can be service enumeration, noisy but effective reconnaissance, connection table exhaustion, reduced availability, and a weaker ability to distinguish benign traffic from hostile probing. (Sources: nhimg.org/glossary/synack/)
22396  26.608189   192.168.127.126 192.168.127.6   TCP 60  61202 → 445 [RST] Seq=1 Win=0 Len=0 #### TCP SYN (Stealth) scan SYN scan is the default and most popular scan option. - Can be performed quickly, scanning thousands of ports per second on a fast network not hampered by intrusive firewalls. - SYN scan is relatively unobtrusive and stealthy, since it never completes TCP connections. (SYN scan may be requested by passing the -sS option to Nmap.)
If the SYN/ACK is ignored completely, target will assume it was dropped and keep re-sending it. The proper response is, since we don’t want to make a full connection, is a RST packet. This tells the target to forget about (reset) the attempted connection. Because the three-way handshake is never completed, SYN scan is sometimes called half-open scanning. (Sources: Nmap)



Port 445 is a network port used by the SMB protocol that is integral to accessing shared resources on a network. SMB operatesat the application layer and allows nodes within a network to communicate, share files, and utilise shared services like printers and access to shared directories. Its role is foundational for intra-network communication and resource sharing, particularly in Windows-operated network environments. (Sources: SecurityScorecard)

title: Verbose Potato
text:
UDP port 4000
The Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) registers port 4000 for terabase. (Sources: AuditMyPC)


UDP port 1947
In practice, port 1947 belongs to Sentinel HASP(Hardware Against Software Piracy), a hardware-based software licensing system used by thousand of commercial applications worldwide.
Common on corporate networks, engineering workstations, and any environment where expensive specialised software is licensed per-seat.

What Actually Runs Here
A vendor ships their software with a USB dongle (the hardware key). When the software starts, it contacts the HASP License Manager running on your machine – or on a license server across the network – to verify the dongle is present and the license is valid. Without that confirmation, the software refuses to run. Port 1947 is the address of that conversation.
The protocol uses both TCP and UDP: - UDP 1947: Broadcast discovery (“Is there a license server out there?”) - TCP 1947: Once a server is found, all actual license communication moves here. (Sources: Connected Systems)

title: STP (Spanning Tree Protocol)
text:
Spanning tree is the family of IEEE 802.1 protocols that stops Ethernet frames from circling forever when switches are wired with redundant links. Every bridge exchanges small messages called BPDUs, the network elects one root bridge, and each bridge blocks just one enough ports that exactly one loop free path remains between any two points.
(Sources: Safeguard)




The bridge on the network that serves as a central point in the spanning tree



The port on each device that provides the most efficient path to the device
(Sources: Cisco Systems)

title: PROFINET IO (PN-IO)
text:
A fieldbus protocol for decentralised Input/Output. (Sources: Wireshark Wiki) ## fieldbus protocol A digital, serial, multi-drop, two-way data bus or communication path or link between low-level industrial field equipment such as sensors, transducers, actuators, local controllers, and even control room devices.

Multi-Drop Bus (MDB) – what is different from general buses? A computer bus able to connect three or more devices. A process of arbitration determines which device sends information at any point. The other devices listen for the data they are intended to receive.
Multidrop buses have the advantage of simplicity and extensibility, but their differing electrical characteristics make them relatively unsuitable for high frequency or high bandwidth applications. (Sources: Wikipedia - Multidrop bus)
Transducer Capabilities: provide the ability for computing devices to interact directly with physical entities of interest. The two types: sensing and actuating (Sources: NIST GLOSSARY)



Use of fieldbus technologies eliminates the need for point-to-point wiring between the controller and each device. A protocol is used to define messages over the fieldbus network, and each message identifies a particular sensor on the network. (Sources: NIST GLOSSARY)



Traditional centralised systems route all I/O signals back to a main control cabinet housing PLCs or distributed control systems. - Advantage: Programming stays simple because all logic resides in one controller. - Challenges: - Extensive wiring runs increase installation costs: field devices transmit signals over long cable runs to the central controller). - Create potential failure points: signal quality degrades over long distances. Plus, the central controller becomes a single point of failure that can shut down entire production areas. - Usage: - Smaller facilities with I/O points clustered near the control room - Preferred when tight integration between different processes is required


Smart I/O modules with built-in processing power connect directly to field devices and make local decisions. These modules communicate with higher-level controllers through industrial networks like Ethernet/IP or Profinet. - Advantages: - Wiring costs drop dramatically - Response times improve - System reliability increases because failures in one area don’t affect others - Tradeoffs: - Higher upfront costs for intelligent I/O modules compared to simple remote I/O - Network management becomes more complex, requiring expertise in industrial communication protocols (Sources: Global Electronic Services)

title: Loop (Ethernet Configuration Testing Protocol, ECTP)
text:
Functialnality of the protocol is similar to that offered by ping but it operates at the data link layer (Layer 2) as opposed to the network layer.
(Sources: Wikipeia)


The goals of the Ethernet Configuration Testing Protocol specification are:

Provide the required functions to enable all forms of multi-station loop tests that are necessary to diagnose a station’s ability to communicate.
Allow each station to assume the responsibility to diagnose its own ability to communicate.
Allow a network management station to diagnose any other station’s ability to communicate.
Minimise processing and memory requirements.



A station using the Configuration Testing Protocol can ascertain the following: - The ability to communicate with a specific remote station. - The ability to aommunicate with some remote station. - With the help of a third party station, the ability to hear or to be heard by a specific station.
(Sources: mit.edu/people/jhawk/ctp.html)

title: Lab Diagram
text:
Three Control Processes

1. High-speed magnetic levitation process (Maglev)
Maglev (magnetic levitation): a method by which an object is suspended with no support other than magnetic fields (Sources: Wikipedia) - The Maglev system is nonlinear, open-loop, unstable, time-varying, and frictionless - Basic principle of operation is to apply the voltage to an electromagnet to keep a ferromagnetic sphere levitated. - The controller maintains the equilibrium state of two forces (the gravitational and electromagnetic) to keep the sphere at a desired distance from the magnet. - The Process is extremely fast; the controller’s sample time should be as short as 1 ms. (Sources: OT_testbed_description.pdf)


2. MPS FESTO workstation (Factory)
The Factory mimics the industrial processing of parts. The workstation used has binary controls. - Control is performed using valves (coils on the valves) that supply air to the actuators that set them in motion. - On/off type valves are used.

Solenoid valves:
Electromechanical devices engineered to control the flow of liquids or gases automatically. Instead of requiring a human operator to physically turn a handle or adjust a wheel, a solenoid valve uses an electrical signal to open, close, or regulate fluid lines in milliseconds.

How it works:
(Sources: ECAS on YouTube)


When the valve is at rest and no electrical current is running through the coil, the valve is in its de-energised state. In a standard normally closed valve, the return spring pushes the plunger downward. The seal at the bottom of the plunger presses tightly against the valve’s inner opening (orifice). The pressure of the incoming fluid often assists in holding the seal shut. As long as no power is applied, the valve remains completely sealed and no fluid or gas can pass through.
An electric current (direct or alternating) is delivered to the solenoid coil.
Electricity flows through the copper windings and generates a concentrated electromagnetic field through the centre of the coil. This magnetic field acts as a powerful magnet, attracting the ferromagnetic plunger.
The magnetic force overcomes the tension of the return spring, pulling the plunger upward toward the top of the tube.
As the plunger snaps upward, it lifts the seal off the orifice. This clears the central passageway, allowing the fluid or gas to flow through the valve body from the inlet port to the outlet port.
As long as electric power is continuously supplied to the coil, the magnetic field remains active, holding the plunger in the open position against the compressed spring.


The measurement is performed by sensors confirming the position of the item being transported (binary signal).





3. Thermal stand (Heating-cooling)
The user influences the temperature distribution in the facility through controllable fans and heaters. The test bed can be controlled via an automation system using the Modbus communication protocol.
The thermal stand has six manipulated variables: Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) signals that control the fans.

Pulse Width Modulation: any method of representing a signal as a rectangular wave with a varying duty cycle. (Sources: Wikipedia)

Duty cycle: the proportion of ‘on’ time to the regular interval or ‘period’ of time

Expressed in percent, 100% being fully on; when a digital signal is on half of the time and off the other half of the time, the digital signal has a duty cycle of 50% and resembles a “square” wave. The process has seven measured output variables: temperatures in different parts of the system.



The temperature sensors communicate internally using the OneWire bus, while current and voltage measurements use dedicated electronic devices.
All inputs and output signals are available via the Modbus protocol.

title: Modbus/TCP (Modbus TCP/IP)
text:
Modbus messaging structure embedded inside a TCP/IP packet,
Allows industrial devices like PLCs, I/O modules and Modbus gateways to communicate over Ethernet-based or intranet or internet networks
De facto automation standard

PLC: a solid-state control system that has a user-programmable memory for storing instructions for the purpose of implementing specific functions such as I/O control, logic, timing, counting, three mode (PID) control, communication, arithmetic, and data and file processing (Sources: NIST GLOSSARY)




Client (master) sends request to server (slave) devices to read or write data, and the server performs the action and responds back to the client.


Physical node addresses (server IDs) used in serial networks are replaced by a combination of an IP address and an optional Unit ID. - A client routes commands to specific devices by first targeting a unique IP address on the Ethernet network and then specifies a particular server through a Unit ID, once the data arrives. - Unit ID can serve two distinct purposes: ensuring a protocol compliance and routing to serial devices.


When directly connecting Ethernet-native devices, the IP address already provides a unique, direct path between them, making the Unit ID redundant because there is only one device at each location. In practice, the Unit ID is typically set to 0 or 255 to ensure compliance with the Modbus TCP/IP specification. - Using these reserved values ensures the message is processed by the main controller’s application layer rather than being discarded or misinterpreted as an invalid sub-network address. - Most modern Ethernet-native servers are programmed to ignore the Unit ID entirely but setting it to 255 remains the industry-standard safe value for direct communication.



Unit ID acts as a translator between a multi-device serial network and Modbus TCP/IP. - Gateway is assigned a single IP address that represents the entire serial chain. - To target a specific device, the client uses Unit IDs 1 to 247. - This allows each serial server to be individually represented and polled through the same Ethernet connection, using the Unit ID to uniquely identify the destination once the packet reaches the gateway.




Polling: the process of repeatedly sampling the status of external devices by a client program (Sources: TechTarget)
This protocol allows for simultaneous communication by opening multiple TCP sockets at once, so a client can poll several different IP addresses at once rather than waiting for each device in a row But every server has a physical hardware limit on how many sockets it can maintain. (If a client attempts to open more sockets than the hardware supports, server will reject the connection.)
Because the protocol itself operates on a request-response basis, every command sent by the client must have a corresponding response from the server to confirm the transaction regardless of how many sockets are open.////////


While a client can poll multiple gateways simultaneously, the devices behind a single gateway must still be polled sequentially. Because the gateway must translate the Ethernet message back into a serial broadcast, the RS-485 daisy chain still uses half-duplex (one-at-a-time) communication. If a client sends multiple requests to different Unit IDs on the same gateway too quickly, the gateway will buffer those requests and send them out one by one.
(Sources: Real Time Automation)

title: DIAL Service Discovery
text:
DIAL–for DIscovery And Launch– is a simple protocol that second-screen devices can use to discover and launch apps on first-screen devices. (Sources: DIAL) - Removes the pain of having to launch the required app on the first-screen before interacting with it from their second-screen. - Only requirement is that both first and second-screens are connected to the same home network. (Sources: NCSC)



alt text


A DIAL client that wishes to discover DIAL servers SHALL send an M-SEARCH request over UDP to the IPv4 multicast address 239.255.255.250 and UDP port 1900 including the Search Target header (ST)
urn:dial-multiscreen-org:service:dial:1
(Sources: Netflix, DIAL protocol specification Version 1.6.4)


The “M-” prefix indicates the request is a “mandatory” request within the HTTP Extension Framework.


Defines the scope of extension.



Seconds to delay response



Identify the specific type of device or service a client is searching for on a local network

title: SSDP (Simple Service Discovery Protocol)
text:
A network protocol, associated with the Internet protocol suite for advertisement and discovery of network services and presence information. It accomplishes this without the assistance of server-based configuration mechanisms, such as DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) or DNS (Domain Name System). SSDP is the basis of the discovery protocol of Universal Plug and Play (UPnP) and is intended for use in residential or small office environments.

Universal Plug and Play (UPnP): Permits networked devices to seamlessly discover each other’s presence on the network and establish functional network services.

UPnP assumes the network runs IP, and then uses HTTP on top of IP to provide device/service description, actions, data transfer and event notification.
Device search requests and advertisements are supported by running HTTP on top of UDP (port 1900) using multicast (known as HTTPMU).
Response to search requests are also sent over UDP, but are instead sent using unicast (known as HTTPU)
UPnP devices are plug-and-play in that, when connected to a network, they automatically establish working configurations with other devices, removing the need for users to manually configure and add devices through IP addresses.




SSDP is a text-based protocol based on HTTPU, which uses UDP as the underlying transport protocol.

Services are announced by the hosting system with multicast addressing to a specifically designated IP multicast address at UDP port number 1900.



SSDP uses the HTTP method NOTIFY to announce the establishment or withdrawal of services (presence) information to the multicast group.
A client that wishes to discover available services on a network uses method M-SEARCH Responses to such search requests are sent via unicast addressing to the originating address and port number of the multicast request.
(Sources: Wikipedia)

Modbus TCP/IP clients and servers listen and receive Modbus message over Ethernet via port 502.
(Sources: Introduction to Modbus TCP/IP)

title: Attack methods
text: (README.txt) Nmap ping scan of test bed ICS network (Industrial Control System network) using various modes: from Insane (-T5) to Sneaky (-T1). Traffic gathered from central switch. If scan is very long, trace is stopped after 10 minutes.

title: Attack methods
text:
Nmap Timing Templates (-T)
Allow user to specify how aggressive they wish to be, while leaving Nmap to pick the exact timing values. (Sources: Nmap.org)

Template names: paranoid (0), sneaky (1), polite (2), normal (3), aggressive (4), and insane (5)

The first two are for IDS evasion
Polite (2) slows down the scan to use less bandwidth and target machine resources
Aggressive (4) speeds scans up by making the assumption that you are on a reasonably fast and reliable network.
Insane (5) assumes that you are on an extraordinarily fast network or ar willing to sacrifice some accuracy for speed.
